goal.objective: Track only the work requested in this conversation: build and test bounded GNOME multi-window tools for stable window IDs, verified activation, placement/tiling, and multi-window layouts, with fresh single-use preview tokens and no unsafe Shell evaluation, blind hotkeys, or security bypasses. Obtain separate explicit approval before installing or enabling the GNOME compositor bridge or restarting services. Then remake this repository's README demo from genuine simultaneous footage of a clean OpenCode session beside the applications it controls, using the inspected official OpenCode demo's deliberate zooms, transitions, and readable pacing. Use sample email and signed-out public browsing only; do not send mail, purchase, or publish. Present a short composition/motion preview for approval before replacing the main demo. Update the relevant canonical desktop and README/GIF skills and documentation, preserve this repo's branding, and keep the human-facing root README under 170 physical lines. Verify real outcomes and distinguish source tests from live acceptance. Preserve unrelated dirty work and exclude work from other sessions/windows, including their handoff, goal-docs, orchestration, and configuration changes. Do not commit or push without separate explicit approval.

plan.summary: Add reliable, approval-gated multi-window control, then produce a polished real OpenCode-plus-app demo and update the relevant skills and short README. Exclude unrelated work from other windows/sessions.
completionCriteria: Typed desktop tools identify current-workspace windows unambiguously and support verified focus, placement/tiling, and bounded multi-window layouts through a reviewed GNOME bridge, with fresh single-use previews, explicit permission checks, protected-state refusals, and meaningful tests.

No GNOME bridge installation/activation, permission change, or service restart occurs without separate explicit user approval; live focus and geometry are verified on the approved disposable demo windows before relying on the tools.

The replacement demo shows a real clean OpenCode window alongside the real applications it controls, recorded simultaneously without fabricated chat/tool calls, using deliberate zooms, transitions, and readable pacing informed by the inspected OpenCode reference.

The user approves a short composition/motion preview before the main README demo is replaced; the final GIF decodes correctly, loops, shows completed useful actions, and has a non-animated alternative and honest sample-data/editing disclosures.

Relevant canonical skills, catalog entries, and focused documentation reflect the new tooling and demo requirements; the branded human-facing root README remains under 170 physical lines and its links/assets are verified.

Source tests, real desktop acceptance, and desktop/narrow light/dark README checks are documented accurately. Unrelated dirty work is preserved, other-session work is not tracked or altered, and nothing is committed, pushed, or published without separate approval.

decisions: Only this conversation's work is in scope. Do not incorporate unrelated handoff, goal-docs, orchestration, global configuration, or other-window work.
The old CLI prototype and app-only GIFs are preserved but rejected as the target design; do not mark them as completion of the new demo.
